discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of single electron spins in diamond and their development into nanoscale quantum sensors
subfield: Quantum physics / solid-state quantum sensing (condensed matter and atomic physics)
motivation: Wrachtrup first showed optical readout and coherent control of a single electron spin at room temperature, in the nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre in diamond. This turned an isolated solid-state defect into an addressable quantum system. Lukin and Walsworth, with Wrachtrup, then showed how the NV spin's long coherence could be used for magnetometry with nanoscale resolution and single-spin sensitivity. Together they realised quantum sensing of magnetic fields, temperature and electric fields inside cells, materials and devices, working under ambient conditions. The work created a new field. Solid-state spin defects are now standard tools for imaging magnetism in 2D materials and superconductors, for nanoscale NMR and for biological imaging, and they are the basis of the first quantum networking nodes. It also set off a worldwide search for new spin-qubit hosts. In a clear, transformative way, fragile quantum coherence became a practical measurement technology.
